ch22.note: A 'muffled gourd' (闷葫芦, men hulu) is a sealed gourd whose contents cannot be seen—a stock image for a baffling riddle; 'to open half the muffled gourd' is to let out only part of the secret.

He Yaozu (贺耀组, 1889–1961) held the directorship of the Bureau of Investigation and Statistics in name; real command of its secret-service work lay, as everyone knew, with the deputy, Dai Li. The book notes this to explain who was nominally over Dai and who actually ran things.

ch22.anchor: hoodwinking heaven and crossing the sea
ch22.note: The idiom man tian guo hai (瞒天过海), 'fool the heavens and cross the sea,' the first of the classical Thirty-Six Stratagems: to accomplish a hidden aim behind a screen of open, ordinary-looking conduct that lulls the watcher.

An allusion to Mencius: a soldier who ran fifty paces from the battle mocked one who ran a hundred—yet both had fled. The two differ only in degree, not in kind; neither has any ground to despise the other.

'Peaceful night' (平安夜) is the ordinary Chinese name for Christmas Eve, literally 'night of peace,' after the carol 'Silent Night.' Chen sets the phrase in pointed quotation marks because a killing was carried out on that supposedly peaceful night.

ch22.anchor: the brave man who severs his own wrist
ch22.note: The idiom zhuang shi duan wan (壮士断腕): a bold man whose wrist is bitten by a viper cuts off his own hand to keep the poison from his heart—a painful but resolute sacrifice, a clean break made without flinching.
